title: Quentin and the Songbook
premise: Eleven years ago, cellist Quentin Lockridge walked off a stage mid-concert and out of the life he'd built with composer Ada Ferreira, choosing duty to his family's failing ferry line over love. When his mother's estate yields an unopened letter Ada wrote him the week after he left, Quentin returns to the island town of Salt Hollow, where Ada now runs the summer music festival he abandoned. As the ferry season's final crossing approaches, Quentin must decide whether to perform again—and whether to ask Ada to stay when the last boat leaves. He plays the festival's closing night, and Ada chooses the last ferry of the season not as an exit but as the place where they finally meet each other halfway.
about_author: Mirabel Oyelaran is a former orchestra librarian who spent six summers working ticket booths on a coastal ferry line, collecting the love stories of strangers who missed their boats on purpose. She writes from a converted boathouse, where she keeps a broken metronome on her desk as a reminder that timing is everything.

chapters.title: The Unopened Postmark
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sorting his late mother's belongings in Salt Hollow, Quentin finds a letter addressed to him, postmarked eleven years ago—the week after he fled. His hands shake too badly to open it. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; the past has been waiting patiently, and so, apparently, has he.

chapters.title: Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with flashback. He recalls the catastrophic final performance—his bow arm seizing mid-solo, Ada's face in the third row—and the vow he made afterward: train the heart like any muscle, contain it, never let it fail publicly again. Beat: establishing the armor he'll spend the book losing.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Lockridge ferry line runs its final autumn crossing; Quentin, now nominal owner, learns the route may be sold. On board, he glimpses festival posters bearing Ada's name. Beat: two inheritances collide—his mother's boat and the life he refused.

chapters.title: Ada, Third Row
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She spots Quentin at the harbor and feels eleven years compress into a single breath. She's built the festival from the wreckage he left her, and she refuses to be undone by his return. Beat: guarded fury braided with unfinished tenderness.

chapters.title: The Letter He Won't Read
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He carries the letter everywhere but can't break the seal, terrified it will confirm what he suspects: she waited, once. A near-encounter at the festival office ends with both pretending indifference. Beat: avoidance as a full-time occupation.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Room Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The festival needs a cellist for its anniversary program—a piece Ada composed the year he left. Her board pressures her to invite Quentin. She drafts the invitation, burns it, then sends it anyway. Beat: professional necessity weaponized against personal survival.

chapters.title: Yes, Professionally
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He accepts the gig, telling himself it's about saving the ferry line's funding partnership. First rehearsal: his hands hold, barely, and Ada corrects his phrasing like no time has passed. Beat: the muscle holds; everything else trembles.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Stranded by fog after rehearsal, they take shelter in the ferry cabin and trade careful half-truths about the years between. Neither mentions the letter. Beat: intimacy relearning its old language, one cautious word at a time.

chapters.title: The Board's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The sale offer on the ferry line arrives with a deadline: sign before season's end or lose everything. Duty, that old reliable argument, comes knocking again. Beat: history offering him the same choice in a new envelope.

chapters.title: Ada's Unfinished Movement
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We learn the anniversary piece is titled 'For Q.,' written in the raw weeks after he left and never performed. She decides, privately, that if he ever reads the letter, she'll let him hear it. Beat: her own sealed room, waiting.

chapters.title: A Borrowed Evening
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Rehearsal runs long; they share dinner at the dockside diner where they had their first date. Laughter ambushes them both. Walking her home, he almost touches her hand. Beat: hope sneaking past the sentries.

chapters.title: The Rival Crossing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ferry line's prospective buyer turns out to be a developer whose marina project would demolish the festival pavilion. Ada realizes Quentin's signature dooms more than a boat. Beat: stakes entwine; his duty is her demolition.

chapters.title: Midnight Interlude
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Unable to sleep, he practices alone in the empty pavilion; Ada finds him there. They play together for the first time in eleven years, wordless, and afterward stand too close in the dark. Beat: the almost-kiss, interrupted by dawn and cowardice.

chapters.title: What Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. An aunt reveals his mother intercepted Ada's letter all those years ago, believing she was protecting Quentin's future. The betrayal reframes everything: Ada never stopped writing. Beat: grief redirected; the villain was love wearing duty's coat.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alone on the night crossing, he finally opens the letter. Ada wrote that she would wait one year—that if he chose her, she'd be at the last ferry of the following season. He missed it by a decade. Beat: devastation with a door left open in it.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Pavilion
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Quentin tells Ada everything—the interception, the missed year, the sale he hasn't signed. She's furious not at the past but at his habit of deciding alone what's best for everyone. Beat: climax of the emotional arc; love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the buyer's office, pen hovering, Quentin asks for one alteration: the pavilion preserved, the ferry line run as a cooperative with the festival. The buyer balks; Quentin walks. Beat: duty finally bent to serve love instead of replacing it.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Festival opening night; Quentin doesn't appear, and Ada fears she drove him away for good. Then she learns why he was absent—and what he gave up. Beat: the turn from anger toward belief.

chapters.title: Anniversary Program
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Closing night. Quentin takes the stage for 'For Q.,' hands steady, heart anything but contained. Mid-movement, he looks up and plays the rest directly to Ada. Beat: the catastrophic performance redeemed; vulnerability as virtuosity.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Backstage, they finally say the unsaid things—apologies, the intercepted years, the fear neither outgrew. Ada confesses she almost left Salt Hollow this spring; staying felt like losing. Beat: two people choosing visibility over safety.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Departs
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Season's final crossing. Instead of watching Ada sail away, Quentin boards with her—as passenger, partner, and co-signer of the cooperative agreement. They ride the last ferry out and back, just because they can. Beat: the blurb's promise fulfilled; departure transformed into arrival.

chapters.title: Coda: Next Season's Timetable
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, epilogue. Spring: the pavilion restored, the ferry repainted, a new piece on Ada's stand titled 'For Us.' Quentin opens his mother's old logbook and writes the first entry in eleven years. Beat: inheritance reclaimed—memory kept, love stayed, the heart trained at last to remain.
